A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved from v2's appendices into v3's main text.

before.justification: Despite being a survey, v2 reports its own LSMOP1 experiment: Appendix B specifies 5,000 iterations per algorithm, with resulting solution distributions in Figures 4 and 7.

after.justification: Section 4 and Figure 5 retain original LSMOP1 solution distributions obtained after 5,000 iterations per algorithm. Retained experimental results qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The surveyed algorithm procedures and architecture families are retained. Neither version introduces a proposed algorithm, and the terminology and exposition edits do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The original evaluation remains the same two-objective LSMOP1 problem. The benchmark catalog in Table 3 is unchanged; moving dataset descriptions into Section 8.1 does not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The reported LSMOP1 comparison drops PMGDA, UMOD, and Smooth Tchebycheff, previously evaluated in Appendix B/Figure 7. MGDA, PMTL, EPO, GradHV, and MOO-SVGD remain in v3 Figure 5.

E3.justification: The retained LSMOP1 experiment uses the same two-objective setting and 5,000-iteration budget. V3 moves this budget from Appendix B into Section 4 without reporting a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The qualitative case study of solution diversity and preference alignment loses the PMGDA, UMOD, and Smooth Tchebycheff diagnostic plots. Its principal contrasts remain illustrated by the five retained methods; no new robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the LSMOP1 illustration.

E6.justification: Three solution-distribution results are removed, including the illustrated PMGDA exact-alignment finding. The five retained plots contain unchanged plotted data, and the convergence results in Table 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the positive-weight, convex-objective KKT characterization from a sufficient condition to a sufficient and necessary condition for Pareto optimality. This strengthens a mathematical statement without an accompanying derivation; the principal definitions, theorem, and convergence analysis remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a first comprehensive survey of gradient-based multi-objective deep learning, organized around single, finite, and infinite solution outputs and covering theory and applications. The rewritten abstract and conclusion retain this contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes the interpretation of MOO-SVGD's first term from guiding solutions toward the Pareto set to driving particles toward a target distribution. Section 3.3 also describes speedup-related performance costs more strongly. Most limitations and future directions are retained.

D1.justification: Dataset details from Appendix C move into Section 8.1, while the algorithm-list, LibMTL, and LibMOON access information and library capabilities remain unchanged. No new implementation, hardware, or experimental hyperparameter information is supplied.

R1.justification: V3 retains the earlier cited works and adds ten references, principally supporting classical optimization background, gradient-free methods, fairness, and PARM. The comparison with prior surveys and claimed novelty remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The introduction's organization changes, notation guidance expands, and appendix explanations and dataset descriptions are integrated into the main narrative, alongside numerous local wording edits.

P2.justification: The document switches from a two-column IEEE-style layout to a single-column ACM-style layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, figures and tables are reformatted, and v3 Figure 5 combines v2 Figure 4 with the appendix MGDA panel while omitting three other panels.

improvement.justification: V3 improves accessibility through clearer introductory framing and integration of the Pareto illustration and dataset descriptions. However, it narrows the illustrative comparison and strengthens the positive-weight KKT statement to necessity without further justification. With the central survey and retained results otherwise stable, these presentation benefits and technical concerns leave the net quality change uncertain.
